title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
statement: Return the number of nodes along the longest path from the root down to a leaf (0 for an empty tree). Trees are given as level-order lists with None for missing children.

hints.1_question: The depth of a tree depends on the depths of its two subtrees. What is the depth of an empty tree?
hints.2_nudge: Recursion: depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)), with depth(None) = 0.
hints.3_big_hint: if not root: return 0; return 1 + max(maxDepth(root.left), maxDepth(root.right)).

known_bugs.name: counts all nodes
known_bugs.followup: Depth is the longest root-to-leaf path. Does adding both subtrees measure that?

known_bugs.name: only follows left children
known_bugs.followup: What if the only child of the root is on the right?

known_bugs.name: uses min instead of max
known_bugs.followup: A node with one child: what is min(depth(left), depth(right)) when one side is empty?

followups: How would you compute it iteratively with a queue (BFS)?
